GraphGAN is an implicit generative model for graphs that learns to mimic real-world networks by modeling the distribution of biased random walks. The paper introduces SRatio, a method that enhances simple models by reweighting training data using information from complex models like deep neural networks. Unlike previous works, SRatio also considers the simple model's per-sample hardness estimates. The method is applied to various classifiers and shows improved performance on multiple datasets, often matching or approaching the performance of complex models. Theoretical analysis supports the approach by demonstrating that the weighted loss of simple models using SRatio upper bounds the loss of the complex model.

The paper introduces a new second-order optimization method called CurveBall for deep learning, which is computationally efficient and easy to implement. Unlike traditional second-order solvers, CurveBall avoids the costly inversion of the Hessian matrix by maintaining a single estimate of the gradient projected by the inverse Hessian, updated with just two forward passes per iteration. This method is validated on small problems and large models like ResNet and VGG-f, showing faster convergence without hyperparameter tuning and demonstrating generality across various architectures.

The effectiveness and robustness of isomax are demonstrated through experiments on classification and clustering tasks.

The approach is validated on datasets like MNIST, Omniglot, and CIFAR-10, showing improvements over existing methods.

1755
The study introduces the Displaced Rectifier Linear Unit (DReLU) activation function, designed to improve compatibility with batch normalization in deep networks. Experiments on VGG and Residual Networks using CIFAR-100 and CIFAR-10 datasets show that DReLU speeds up learning and enhances test accuracy compared to other activation functions like ReLU, LReLU, PReLU, and ELU.
-----
-----
524
The paper connects Distributional RL with the Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) method for exploration. It introduces a new algorithm using truncated variance, which improves performance in multi-armed bandits and Atari 2600 games compared to QR-DQN.
-----
-----
257
The paper addresses the challenge of Unseen Class Categorization (UCC) in machine learning, where minimal information is available about target classes. Existing methods struggle with either feature extraction or classifier adaptability. The proposed solution involves network reparameterization to decouple feature extraction and classification, enhancing both discriminability and adaptability. Experiments show state-of-the-art performance in zero-shot and few-shot learning settings.
-----
-----
2014
The paper introduces a method to train Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) with discrete latent variables, such as binary or categorical values, by using a differentiable estimator for the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) based on importance sampling. This approach addresses the challenge posed by the inability to use reparametrized sampling with discrete variables. The method is validated through experiments on two different VAE architectures and benchmark datasets.
-----
-----
1669
This paper introduces the Distribution Matching Prototypical Network (DMPN) for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA), which models deep features as Gaussian mixtures to explicitly measure domain discrepancies. DMPN uses two novel domain discrepancy losses and is trained to minimize both classification and domain discrepancy losses. It achieves significant improvements in digit image transfer tasks and a mean accuracy of 81.4% on the VisDA 2017 dataset, demonstrating robustness to hyper-parameter changes.
-----
-----
2333
The paper introduces the Integrative Tensor-based Anomaly Detection (ITAD) framework for detecting anomalies in satellite systems, using telemetry data from KOMPSAT-2. By applying CANDECOMP/PARAFAC decomposition to construct 3rd-order tensors, the method aims to improve accuracy and reduce false positives compared to traditional approaches.
-----
-----
702
The paper introduces State Space LSTM (SSL), a model that combines the strengths of LSTM and state space models without making factorization assumptions. It uses an efficient sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) method for inference, demonstrating superior performance and stability across various domains.
-----
-----
796
The paper introduces spectral normalization, a lightweight technique to stabilize the training of the discriminator in generative adversarial networks (GANs). Tested on CIFAR10, STL-10, and ILSVRC2012 datasets, spectrally normalized GANs (SN-GANs) produce high-quality images, matching or exceeding previous stabilization methods.

-----
1576
The paper focuses on enhancing the stability of machine learning models against input perturbations. It introduces a computationally efficient Jacobian regularization method to increase classification margins in neural networks. This approach improves robustness against both random and adversarial input perturbations while maintaining good generalization on clean data.
-----
-----
1114
The paper addresses the challenges of expensive annotations and diminishing sample informativeness in supervised deep learning by proposing a novel training framework. This framework adaptively selects informative samples based on a hardness-aware strategy in a latent space constructed by a generative model. Experiments on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and IVUS datasets show that this approach outperforms random sampling, highlighting its effectiveness.
-----
-----
2513
The paper introduces Past Decode Regularization (PDR), a new method for regularizing LSTMs in language modeling. PDR improves next-token prediction by biasing the model to retain more contextual information. It achieves state-of-the-art results on Penn Treebank and WikiText-2 datasets with minimal overhead, and further improves performance when combined with a mixture of softmaxes. Additionally, PDR shows strong performance in character-level language modeling on the Penn Treebank Character dataset.
-----
-----
254
The paper introduces Morph-Net, a neural network that uses morphological operations (dilation and erosion) instead of traditional linear combinations and activation functions. This approach allows Morph-Net to approximate smooth functions with fewer parameters and perform well on datasets like MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100.
-----
-----
327
The paper explores consistency regularization in semi-supervised learning, highlighting its benefits and challenges with Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). It introduces Stochastic Weight Averaging (SWA) and fast-SWA to improve convergence and achieve state-of-the-art results on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets, significantly reducing error rates with limited labeled data.

1789
The paper introduces two semi-supervised graph-based dependency parsing models: Local Autoencoding Parser (LAP) and Global Autoencoding Parser (GAP). Both models use deep neural networks for encoding and generative models for decoding, with LAP using sequential latent variables and GAP using dependency trees. Experiments on WSJ and UD datasets show improved performance with limited labeled data by leveraging unlabeled data.

-----
505
The study compares six unsupervised disentanglement methods (Beta-VAE, Factor-VAE, DIP-I-VAE, DIP-II-VAE, Info-VAE, and Beta-TCVAE) on the mpi3d dataset. Beta-TCVAE performed best according to metrics like DCI, Factor-VAE, IRS, MIG, and SAP-Score, but qualitative analysis showed inconsistent correlation between metrics and actual disentanglement.

-----
979
The study compares generic and modular models for grounded language understanding, focusing on their ability to generalize systematically. Modular models show better generalization but are sensitive to module layout. End-to-end methods often fail to learn effective layouts for systematic generalization, suggesting that additional regularizers or priors may be necessary.

1306
The paper introduces a method for learning dependencies between latent variables in deep latent variable models by combining deep generative models and probabilistic graphical models. It uses a variational autoencoder (VAE) with a Bayesian network to represent the latent variable space and optimizes network parameters, variational parameters, and latent topology simultaneously. The framework is validated on datasets like MNIST, Omniglot, and CIFAR-10, showing improvements over existing structured variational autoencoder baselines.

1155
The paper introduces the Unrestricted Recursive Network (URN), which can dynamically adapt its structure during training, mimicking the flexibility of biological neural networks. The URN can evolve into various common neural network architectures, such as fully connected, locally connected, and residual networks, based on the data structure and regulator terms in a single general loss function. This adaptability is driven by gradient descent and is influenced by the network's symmetries and the geometric properties of the input data.
-----
-----
2288
The paper compares Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational AutoEncoders (VAEs), highlighting that VAEs use an explicit probability model while GANs do not, which limits their use in statistical inference. The study introduces an optimal transport GAN with entropy regularization, showing it can maximize a lower-bound on average sample likelihoods, similar to VAEs. This approach allows GANs to compute likelihood statistics, and numerical results support the proposed theory.

The paper compares Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational AutoEncoders (VAEs), highlighting that VAEs use an explicit probability model while GANs do not. The authors introduce an optimal transport GAN with entropy regularization, showing it can maximize a lower-bound on average sample likelihoods, similar to VAEs. 2514
The paper introduces Past Decode Regularization (PDR), a new method for regularizing LSTMs in language modeling. PDR improves next-token prediction by biasing the model to retain more contextual information. It achieves state-of-the-art results on Penn Treebank and WikiText-2 datasets with minimal overhead. Additionally, PDR enhances performance when combined with a mixture-of-softmaxes and excels in character-level language modeling on the Penn Treebank Character dataset.

-----
572
The paper introduces iTM-VAE, a Bayesian nonparametric topic model using variational auto-encoders, which can adapt the number of topics to data and offers efficient inference through neural networks. Two variants, iTM-VAE-Prod and iTM-VAE-G, are proposed for enhanced performance and automatic concentration parameter adjustment. Experiments on 20News and Reuters RCV1-V2 datasets demonstrate superior performance in perplexity, topic coherence, and document retrieval tasks.

73
The paper investigates the structure of neural network loss functions and their impact on generalization. It introduces a "filter normalization" method to visualize loss function curvature and compares different loss functions. The study also examines how network architecture and training parameters influence the loss landscape and the shape of minimizers.

2672
The paper addresses the issue of mislabeled examples in large datasets, which can harm the generalization of over-parameterized neural networks. It introduces On-the-fly Data Denoising (ODD), a method that uses stochastic gradient descent with large learning rates to identify and discard mislabeled examples based on loss statistics, effectively improving model performance with minimal computational overhead.

-----
852
The paper explores image captioning using a conditional GAN framework, introducing a context-aware LSTM captioner and a co-attentive discriminator to align image and caption semantics. It compares Self-critical Sequence Training (SCST) and Gumbel Straight-Through (ST) methods, finding SCST to be more stable and effective.

416
The paper introduces an adaptive convolution method for GANs to improve image generation by learning upsampling based on local context, outperforming traditional methods on CIFAR-10 and STL-10 datasets.

2190
The paper introduces iterative regularized dual averaging (iRDA), a method to enhance the efficiency of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by reducing model redundancy without sacrificing accuracy. Tested on datasets like MNIST and CIFAR-10, iRDA outperforms existing compression techniques, achieving over 95% weight reduction while maintaining accuracy. Notably, a ResNet18 model with 95% sparsity using iRDA matches the performance of a larger ResNet50 model
